decisions.reason: Dampsoft publicly announced the digital anamnesis app as its new product line, invested in it heavily, and placed it at the centre of its digitalization direction, so management will persist with it and treat any weak uptake as temporary.

The continuing education institute builds on the firm's long-standing ties to the dental community, and the pandemic offers a convenient temporary explanation for weak attendance, so management keeps it rather than admit the investment failed.
The remote screen-sharing tool is a low-cost support utility woven into service delivery and grew more useful under remote work, so there is little reason to drop it.
The analytics dashboard got its own page and fits the announced data-driven practice software strategy, so the visible commitment and sunk development cost argue for keeping and improving it.
The complete practice bundle was promoted prominently as a flagship offering, so management is likely to keep it, perhaps repackaged, rather than reverse a publicly backed decision.

The job and practice listing portal is peripheral and was only mentioned on the site, making it the most expendable product, but its low running cost and fit with the dental ecosystem still lead management to keep it for now.
